signature.name: Faneuil Hall Marketplace
signature.detail: A historic market and meeting hall that has been a gathering place since the 1740s, now filled with shops and food stalls. It is a must-see for its role in the American Revolution and lively atmosphere. Tip: visit on a weekday morning to avoid crowds and enjoy the street performers.

signature.name: USS Constitution
signature.detail: The world's oldest commissioned naval vessel still afloat, launched in 1797 and famous for its role in the War of 1812. Tours are led by Navy sailors and include the story of 'Old Ironsides'. Tip: the ship is free to visit but requires a timed ticket from the Charlestown Navy Yard visitor center; go early as lines form quickly.

signature.name: Boston Common
signature.detail: America's oldest public park, dating back to 1634, and the starting point of the Freedom Trail. It offers a green escape in the heart of the city and hosts seasonal events. Tip: combine with a walk through the adjacent Public Garden for the best experience.

signature.name: Freedom Trail
signature.detail: A 2.5-mile red-brick path connecting 16 significant historical sites, from Boston Common to Bunker Hill. It is the best way to see the city's revolutionary history in one go. Tip: wear comfortable shoes and start early; guided tours are available but the trail is self-guided and free.

signature.name: Fenway Park
signature.detail: Home of the Boston Red Sox, this is one of the most iconic ballparks in America, opened in 1912. Even non-baseball fans enjoy the historic atmosphere and the Green Monster. Tip: take a guided tour on non-game days to see the press box and dugout.

signature.name: Museum of Fine Arts
signature.detail: One of the largest art museums in the United States, with a collection spanning ancient to contemporary art, including works by Rembrandt, Monet, and Van Gogh. It is a must for art lovers. Tip: visit on a weekday afternoon for fewer crowds; the museum is easily reached by the Green Line E train.

signature.name: New England Aquarium
signature.detail: A leading aquarium featuring a massive central tank with sharks, sea turtles, and thousands of fish, plus penguin exhibits and a IMAX theater. It is a favorite for families. Tip: buy tickets online in advance to skip the line, and go early in the day.

signature.name: Harvard Square
signature.detail: The vibrant heart of Cambridge, home to Harvard University and a mix of historic buildings, bookstores, and cafes. It offers a glimpse of college life and intellectual history. Tip: take the Red Line to Harvard station and wander the yard; free student-led tours are often available.

signature.name: Old North Church
signature.detail: Boston's oldest church, famous for the lanterns that signaled Paul Revere's midnight ride in 1775. It is a key stop on the Freedom Trail. Tip: check opening hours as they vary seasonally; a small donation is suggested for entry.

signature.name: Boston Tea Party Ships & Museum
signature.detail: An interactive museum where you can throw tea overboard and learn about the pivotal event leading to the American Revolution. It is engaging for all ages. Tip: book tickets online for a specific time slot, as tours are timed.
